newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: OLYMPICS-CAPE TOWN GETS AFRICAN BACKING.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-CAPE TOWN GETS AFRICAN BACKING.

text.p: Africa's umbrella sports body has endorsed the bid by Cape Town to host the 2004 Olympic Games, the city's bid committee said on Tuesday.

"The Supreme Council for Sport in Africa (SCSA) pledge of support strongly reinforces our efforts to bring the Olympic Games to Africa for the first time," Cape Town Olympic bid chairman Chris Ball told a news conference.
Ball presented a statement from the SCSA saying: "The Cape Town 2004 Olympic Bid is a candidature for the whole of Africa."
But Ball said the endorsement did not mean all 20 African executive members of the 106-member International Olympic Committee would vote in Cape Town's favour.

The 12 cities bidding to host the 2004 games were visited last year by an IOC evaluation commission. The IOC will announce a shortlist of four cities in March -- with Cape Town, Rio de Janeiro, Athens and Rome often mentioned as front-runners -- and the winning city will be named in September.
